title: Static Pruning
summary: Compare proxy-based EL2N scoring with other coreset methods in terms of cost, signal, and validation needs.

blocks.md:
By the end of this lesson you should be able to:

- Compare proxy-based EL2N scoring with other coreset methods in terms of cost, signal, and validation needs
- Analyze the computational scaling benefits of MinHash and Locality-Sensitive Hashing for web-scale deduplication
- Evaluate the systems and statistical trade-offs of aggressive near-duplicate filtering
- Identify EL2N from its mathematical definition and explain why proxy-based use still requires validation

blocks.source: Vol I, Data Selection, § Static Pruning
blocks.md: Web-scale scraping routinely gathers boilerplate text, duplicate images, and malformed records, and each one costs GPT-2 six FLOPs per parameter for every token, or ResNet-50 a full forward and backward pass, before a single useful gradient is calculated. Static pruning removes these low-value records upstream of the training loop. By dropping redundant and corrupt records before target-model training begins, static pruning shrinks the operation count (Operations) without changing model architectures or execution kernels.

blocks.title: What the section covers
blocks.md:
In the book this section runs through:

- The case for smaller datasets
- Data deduplication
- Data pruning by quality
- Coreset selection algorithms

Pay attention to: Proxy-based coreset scoring; MinHash and LSH deduplication; Validating near-duplicate removal; EL2N.

questions.q: A team wants to score a dataset cheaply before training a large production model. They plan to train a small proxy for a few epochs and rank examples by prediction error, knowing that confidently wrong predictions can still score highly. Which method best matches that plan and its trade-off?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. EL2N ranks samples by early prediction error $\lVert \hat{\mathbf{y}}-\mathbf{y} \rVert_2$, so a cheap proxy can score examples without a full target-model run. The section also warns that high EL2N can include noisy samples and that transfer from proxy to target is useful but not guaranteed. Geometry-based $k$-Center is not label-aware boundary scoring, Forgetting Events is much more expensive, and Herding still depends on feature representations.
questions.hint: Think about: compare proxy-based EL2N scoring with other coreset methods in terms of cost, signal, and validation needs.
options: $k$-Center clustering on raw pixel inputs, because it guarantees zero-cost label-aware boundary identification
Forgetting Events scoring on the full production model, because it requires no proxy architecture and computes in $\mathcal{O}(1)$ time
EL2N (Error L2-Norm) scoring with a briefly trained proxy model, accepting that high error can reflect hard examples or noise
Herding on Gaussian-distributed features, because it completely avoids computing feature representations

questions.q: Why is Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH) with MinHash preferred over exhaustive pairwise Jaccard similarity comparison for large-scale text deduplication?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Comparing all pairs in a dataset of $D$ documents requires $\mathcal{O}(D^2)$ comparisons, which is computationally intractable for web-scale datasets ($D \ge 10^7$). MinHash compresses documents into fixed-size sketches where collision probability equals Jaccard similarity, and LSH bands these sketches into hash buckets so only candidate pairs colliding in a bucket are compared. MinHash LSH does not detect cross-lingual semantic paraphrases, still requires shingling/tokenization, and pairwise Jaccard comparison is an exact set operation rather than a deep learning method.
questions.hint: Think about: analyze the computational scaling benefits of MinHash and Locality-Sensitive Hashing for web-scale deduplication.
options: MinHash LSH guarantees \$100\% precision in detecting semantic paraphrases across different natural languages
MinHash eliminates the need to tokenize or shingle input documents before hashing
Exhaustive pairwise Jaccard comparison requires training a deep neural network, whereas LSH is purely rule-based
Exhaustive pairwise comparison requires $\mathcal{O}(D^2)$ document comparisons, whereas MinHash LSH hashes compact signatures into sublinear candidate collision buckets

questions.q: Removing near-duplicate documents with MinHash LSH always improves model accuracy because duplicate data has zero statistical value in all training regimes.
questions.explanation: False. While deduplication reduces redundant computation and memorization risk, in some domains duplicate frequency reflects natural empirical data distributions or intentional weighting. Aggressive deduplication with miscalibrated thresholds can prune legitimate variations or distort class priors, necessitating empirical validation on downstream accuracy.
questions.hint: Think about: evaluate the systems and statistical trade-offs of aggressive near-duplicate filtering.

questions.q: The training-dynamics coreset metric that measures the Euclidean norm of the difference between predicted class probabilities and the one-hot target vector early in training is known as ____.
questions.explanation: EL2N. It measures $\lVert p(x)-y \rVert_2$ early in training as an error-based difficulty score. The chapter notes that proxy-model rankings can transfer usefully to larger targets, but that transfer must be validated rather than assumed universal.
questions.hint: Think about: identify EL2N from its mathematical definition and explain why proxy-based use still requires validation.
